# FormHelperText accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:start -->

FormHelperText shows a hint or an error message below a field. It is not focusable, so the field covers the keyboard, focus, and pointer criteria.

<!-- intro:end -->

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 12    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 1     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 42    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 3/13  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **4.1.3 Status Messages.** <!-- 4.1.3:gap:start -->The helper text has no live region. A screen reader probably does not announce a new error message until the user moves focus to the field.<!-- 4.1.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- In TextField, the helper text renders after its field in the DOM, so the reading order matches the visual order.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read a form with a screen reader in browse mode.
2. Make sure that each helper text follows its field.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->each helper text follows its field in the reading order.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- Helper text that gives instructions must not rely on position or color alone, such as "see the red text". This is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read each helper text.
2. Make sure that it does not refer to other content only by position or color.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->no helper text relies on position or color alone.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.5 Images of Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

- The helper text is real text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Select the helper text with the mouse.

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->the helper text is real text.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

#### 3.3.3 Error Suggestion · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 3.3.3:start -->

- In the error state, the helper text is the place for a suggestion, for example "Enter a valid email address, for example name@example.com". The author writes it.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Cause an error in a field.
2. Read the error message.

<!-- 3.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.3.3:pass:start -->the message tells the user how to fix the error.<!-- 3.3.3:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormHelperText.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- By default, the root is a `<p>`. The `component` prop can change it. It has no association of its own.
- TextField gives the helper text an `id` and sets `aria-describedby` on its input. A screen reader then reads the helper text as the description. A unit test confirms this. For a non-native select, TextField sets the attribute on the combobox element.
- A standalone FormHelperText inside a `FormControl` gets no association. The author sets an `id` on it and `aria-describedby` on the input. Unit tests confirm both cases.
- With `helperText=" "`, the helper text reserves one line. Its content is an `aria-hidden` zero-width space, so the description is empty.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a TextField with helper text.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Do the test again with a select TextField.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader reads the helper text as the description, after the name of the field.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- In the error state, the helper text turns red. The text of the message also shows the error, so color is not the only cue. The author writes the message.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Put a field in the error state.
2. In Chrome DevTools, open the Rendering tab, and select Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia.
3. Make sure that the words of the message show the error.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->the error message shows the error in words, not only in red.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormHelperText.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ❔

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- The helper text renders below the field, on the page background, in every variant. Its colors in the default theme:

  | State                     | Light mode (`#fff`) | Dark mode (`#121212`) |
  | :------------------------ | ------------------: | --------------------: |
  | Resting, `text.secondary` |              5.74:1 |                9.43:1 |
  | Error, `error.main`       |              4.98:1 |                5.09:1 |
  | Disabled, `text.disabled` |              2.68:1 |                5.32:1 |

- A unit test confirms the resting and error colors in light mode. axe-core `color-contrast` passes on the helper text in both fixtures. On the variants fixture, axe returns `incomplete` for three elements. The empty outlined input has no value to test. The notched outline and the floating label overlap the other outlined input and the `standard` label.
- The helper text of a disabled field is the description of an inactive component, so 1.4.3 does not apply. axe-core cannot see this link and reports a failure, so the fixtures leave out a disabled field. The TextField report takes the same position. A disabled FormHelperText with no disabled field is not exempt.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Open an `outlined`, a `filled`, and a `standard` TextField with helper text.
2. With a contrast checker, measure the helper text of each variant.
3. Put each field in the error state.
4. Measure the error text of each variant.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->the resting and error helper text is at least `4.5:1` in each variant.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 3.3.1 Error Identification · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormHelperText.test.js`

<!-- 3.3.1:start -->

- In the error state, the helper text gives the error in words. InputBase sets `aria-invalid` on the input from the `error` state of the FormControl. A unit test confirms both. The author writes the message.
- `error` without helper text gives only a color cue, as the TextField report notes.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Put a TextField in the error state with helper text.
2. Read the helper text.
3. Make sure that the text names the error in words.

<!-- 3.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.3.1:pass:start -->the helper text names the error in words, for example "Enter a valid email address."<!-- 3.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `form-field-multiple-labels` ✅

<!-- 3.3.2:start -->

- The helper text gives instructions for the field, for example the format. Whether it is clear is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read the helper text of each field that needs a format or a rule.

<!-- 3.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.3.2:pass:start -->each field that needs a format or a rule has helper text that explains it.<!-- 3.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.3 Status Messages · AA

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormHelperText.test.js`

<!-- 4.1.3:start -->

- The helper text is a `<p>` with no `role="status"` and no `aria-live`. A unit test confirms this. The source has no live region, so a screen reader probably does not announce an error message that appears on blur. A review with assistive technology must confirm this.
- When the helper text is the description of the field, the screen reader reads it when the user moves focus back to the field.
- With `helperText=" "`, the `<p>` stays in the page, so an `aria-live` region from the author can work. A helper text that appears with the error cannot.
- To announce the error at once, add a live region in the application.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader.
2. In a field that validates on blur, enter an invalid value.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to the next field.
4. Listen for an announcement of the new error message.

<!-- 4.1.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.3:pass:start -->the screen reader announces the new error. Expected result from the source: it does not.<!-- 4.1.3:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- The helper text uses the `caption` typography, set in `rem`, and wraps. A Playwright test confirms that the standalone fixture does not overflow or clip at a 200% text size.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Open a TextField with long helper text.
2. Set the browser page zoom to 200%.
3. Make sure that the helper text wraps and that no text is cut off.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.4:pass:start -->all helper text is visible at 200% zoom.<!-- 1.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- A long helper text wraps with its container. A Playwright test confirms that the standalone fixture does not scroll horizontally at 320 px.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

#### 1.4.12 Text Spacing · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.12:start -->

- The helper text has no fixed height. A Playwright test applies the WCAG text-spacing values to the standalone fixture and finds no clipped text.

<!-- 1.4.12:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A).** <!-- 1.1.1:start -->The component renders no non-text content of its own. The `" "` placeholder is `aria-hidden`. An icon that the author adds is the author's concern.<!-- 1.1.1:end -->
- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA).** <!-- 1.4.11:start -->The component renders no graphical object and no component boundary of its own.<!-- 1.4.11:end -->
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (A), 2.4.3 Focus Order (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA), 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (A), 2.5.3 Label in Name (A), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA), 3.2.1 On Focus (A), 3.2.2 On Input (A), 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA), 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A).** <!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.1,3.2.2,3.2.4,4.1.2:start -->The helper text is not focusable and has no role or action of its own. The field it describes covers these.<!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,2.5.2,2.5.3,2.5.8,3.2.1,3.2.2,3.2.4,4.1.2:end -->
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** The component renders no links.
- **2.4.6 Headings and Labels (AA).** <!-- 2.4.6:start -->The helper text is not a heading or a label. The field label covers this.<!-- 2.4.6:end -->
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** <!-- 2.5.1,2.5.4:start -->The helper text has no pointer action and reads no device motion.<!-- 2.5.1,2.5.4:end -->
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
